headline: US software company shares have reached new highs for 2026 as fears that AI would wreck their business have faded.
score_reason: Reuters market report read through a copy; event dated 6 Oct 2026, no reduction.
importance_line: Software investors and workers see AI treated more as a help than a threat for now, though one strategist warns that AI coding could become a bigger risk from the second half of 2027.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The American Bazaar, that the S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3% on Tuesday to its highest since November 2025, after its best quarterly gain since 2020, as analysts concluded that fears of an AI-driven "SaaSpocalypse" were overdone. Expected 2026 earnings growth for the sector has risen to 20.6% from 13.8% in March, according to LSEG data, though one strategist said the real test could come in the second half of 2027.
notes: Original Reuters link given; text read on The American Bazaar.
